name: What is the difference between a primary bathroom and an ensuite?

mainEntity.name: Are primary bathroom and ensuite bathroom the same thing, or do they mean different scopes in remodeling?
mainEntity.text: Are primary bathroom and ensuite bathroom the same thing, or do they mean different scopes in remodeling?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most remodeling conversations, primary bathroom and ensuite bathroom mean essentially the same thing: the bathroom attached to the main bedroom. The term primary bathroom is more common in U.S. residential construction and real estate, while ensuite is used more often in other markets. For homeowners, the distinction usually matters less than the actual scope of work. What matters most is whether the bathroom includes a shower, tub, double vanity, separate toilet area, or a larger suite-style layout. Contractors should define the project by square footage, features, and whether plumbing or walls are changing. That avoids confusion when comparing bids. If you are discussing a luxury remodel, the term primary suite may also come up when the bathroom is being designed as part of a larger bedroom-bathroom upgrade.
